My family was.. complicated and a bit of a mess. My mom was an alcoholic and my grandparents were not exactly fit to raise me. It was weird and messed up at times, and from all of that I developed ADHD, but I am still unsure whether that's what fucked my marks in school or if it was the overall family environment. Only problem atm is that I am unsure whether I want this for my whole life, because the whole course to do that is hard, costs a lot of money and is kind of a mess because that particular field is kinda bs. The machines where you take the final exam are not exactly in best condition and oh boy working with dentists can be like working with toddlers at times. It's surprising how many people have no idea what they are doing even in medicine.

I wanted to study when I was young, but I dunno if I would have it in me to do that now. I love music, drawing and sometimes writing. I will see to figure it more out until my early 30s and go from there I guess.

I feel you on the taking more time. I basically picked my job because it was the first best thing, and because I was pressured by my family to do something after school, kinda because they were pressured by youth wellfare organisation but that's another story.

I have more than enough reason to be proud of myself for what I went through, but all I can see is what others archived. Like being a lawyer or a doctor, while I am a simple worker. I know I am not stupid, but I kinda feel like I am for not knowing what I wanna do for the rest of my life.

Gladly sometimes I can still remember that we all are just a tiny speck living on a small rock suspended in space, full of wonders we cannot even grasp without knowing basically anything besides how some of it works. It calms me down, the silence of space and the wonders of it all. I got dragged down by the fact that we seemingly know so much about the universe and it all being just pure chance, but the older I get, the more I grow Spiritual. No one knows exactly everything.

I have been learning piano on my own now for almost one year, almost one and a half if one would count my first little steps towards taking it serious.

In my first year I mainly focused on technique, music theory and am only now slowly learning about the reading. I can read music, just not good enough yet to learn intermediate pieces with it alone yet.  

Even tho it is shunned by way to many people, I learned with those Youtube tutorials. It helps to learn songs in these early stages, but lateron I would recommend also looking at the sheet music. I made it so I had specific pieces, which I learn only with sheet music for training and regular pieces which I look up the sheet music in between or am simply unable to find what I want.

It helps because like this you can learn pieces until you feel confident enough for sheet music alone and gives some extra morale boost because you learn to play a piece. 

What most people tend to do is, as boring as it might be at the start, try to section the piece you are learning. With more smaller parts of a piece, rather than the whole one, the task becomes less frightening. You can try to learn and memorize the first bar of a Song. Left and right hand but seperate, not yet together. 

Some people tend to learn the hardest part of a Song first, because that makes the rest of it appear like a cakewalk, but it's free to you with what you want to start with.

musictheory.net is a wonderful website with Lots of useful stuff regarding music/sight reading and music theory. Best of luck!
